status: DECLARED after the exploration disclosed below and BEFORE the governing run (tools/run_own_motion.py --score), which recomputes every number from scratch on the same 2025 development months and the same twelve-month table. The evidence that does not come from the exploration is the label-free ranking dry run.
mechanism: A departure that the shipped ADS-B matcher does not trace from its gate (dark or unmatched) can still be seen moving: its own aircraft, identified by ICAO address (runs/intruder_identity/ids.parquet, built from the adsb.lol day files, ODbL), blocked in at the departure's own stand as an arrival and later shows ground points moving at >= 3 kt. The matcher's segment starts after the last coverage gap before take-off, so this earlier motion never reaches the features. The first ground motion after the inbound's in-block is not earlier than the off-block in almost every 2025 case with the inbound at the same stand and B <= 2,700 s: label >= B = take-off - that first motion (validity on the twelve 2025 months: EDDF 93.3-99.9%, EGLL 98.4-100%, LFPG 98.8-100% by band). Above 1 h or with a different stand the bound fails (tows, repositioning).

procedure.position: the last layer: v61's chain (runner v55m -> no-NM rematch -> v48's reconciliation -> extreme-day layer -> variance re-allocation -> guarded stacking residual -> intruder stand bound -> identity extension) -> this layer

trigger.identity: the departure's ICAO address is known in the identity table (PHASE DEP)
trigger.inbound: the latest identified arrival of the same ICAO address at the same airport whose in-block precedes the take-off (merge_asof backward on take-off) blocked in 600 s to 64,800 s (10 min to 18 h) before take-off, at the departure's own stand (STAND_mvt equal, both present)
trigger.not_gate_traced: adsb_gate != 1 (src/prc2026_adsb/features.departure_features on the month's matches2 file; dark or unmatched rows)
trigger.first_motion: the first adsb.lol surface point of that ICAO address at that airport with ground = True and gs >= 3 kt strictly after in-block + 120 s (day files of the take-off day and the day before); B = take-off - its time

procedure.value: p + w (B + o(airport) - p); o(airport) = mean of label - B over the fitting months' candidate rows of that airport, shrunk with weight 20 rows to the pooled mean of the three airports; nearest integer (numpy.rint) in the export; no clipping
procedure.fitting_side: candidates of the fitting months from the twelve-month table (runs/daily_totals/rows12.parquet `stack`, the older predictor) after the accepted intruder stand bound and the identity extension, both applied month-blocked exactly as in their governing runs (tools/run_intruder_identity.py accepted_after / fit / values); development month m and twelve-month month m: every other 2025 month; ranking: all twelve 2025 months
procedure.free_parameters: the offsets o only; the airports, 600 s / 64,800 s, 120 s, 3 kt, 60 / 2,700 s and w are fixed here

control.development: the v61 development proxy runs/dig/census61/dev_v61.parquet column `v61` (SHA-256 9739d9c5bfa6258affaf8f9a6db3c001a46c1e1e92308bebcdcd6920c51448de; built by runs/dig/census61/build.py: ctl_v55m `new` -> rematch -> stack_resid_v2 delta -> intruder bound -> identity extension, month-blocked); the governing run requires its month RMSEs to equal runs/dig/census61/steps.json / docs/dig/census61.md exactly
control.twelve: rows12 `stack` after the accepted intruder bound and the identity extension (month-blocked)

rule.text: accepted when (1) no development month (January, July, November, December 2025) is worse than the control by more than 0.005% of its RMSE (all rows); (2) the mean change over the equal-footing months (January, July, December 2025) is at most -0.02%; (3) every equal-footing month's paired-day 95% interval lies below zero; (4) in the twelve-month check every month is better or unchanged
rule.intervals: paired-day bootstrap over UTC take-off days, 2,000 replicates, seed 20261003, relative RMSE change (as tools/run_intruder_bound.py)

exploration_disclosed.tunnel_15: docs/dig/own_bounds.md (closed, c588b91): hard bounds from the departure's own MATCHED segment (block <= motion start on gate rows, block <= first point on dark rows, upper bounds) are either already respected by v61 or invalid where broken (dark first points far older than the off-block: tows, transponder on). This layer differs in source and scope: it uses points found by ICAO identity after the aircraft's own inbound at the same stand, on rows the matcher does not trace from the gate, with B capped at 2,700 s; the long-B rows where tunnel 15's dark bound failed are excluded by the cap and the same-stand inbound requirement.
